title: Systems of Three Linear Equations in Three Variables
seo_title: Algebra II Systems of Three Equations Worksheets (TEKS 2A.3A, 2A.3B)
standard_text: 2A.3A formulate systems of equations, including systems consisting of three linear equations in three variables and systems consisting of two equations, the first linear and the second quadratic; 2A.3B solve systems of three linear equations in three variables by using Gaussian elimination, technology with matrices, and substitution
meta_desc: Free Algebra II worksheets on systems of three linear equations for Texas TEKS 2A.3A and 2A.3B: check ordered triples, elimination, back-substitution, solving and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Eliminate one variable twice, solve the 2 × 2 system, then substitute back.
key_sub: The solution is an ordered triple (x, y, z).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A solution of a system of three equations in x, y and z is an ordered triple (x, y, z) that makes all three equations true.
  • Use two pairs of equations to eliminate the same variable. You get a system of two equations in two variables.
  • Solve it, then substitute back to find the third variable.
  • Gaussian elimination puts the system in a stair shape; then solve from the bottom up (back-substitution).

Examples

Example

x + y + z = 6, y + 2z = 8, z = 3

y = 8 − 6 = 2

x = 6 − 2 − 3 = 1

Answer: (1, 2, 3)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Subtracting when the terms are oppositesAdd 2z and −2z to eliminate z.
Checking only one equationA solution must work in all three.
Mixing up the orderWrite the triple as (x, y, z).

faq.q: What does a system of three equations look like as a graph?
faq.a: Three planes. A single solution is the one point where all three meet.

faq.q: Can a system have no solution?
faq.a: Yes, when the planes have no common point.
